clue.text: Artist texted: "Are you the one whose catch removed Andile P?"

parts.note: in text-message shorthand, 'are you' is written R U, as 'texted' tells us

parts.words: the one whose catch removed Andile P
parts.note: Ben Stokes took the famous one-handed catch that dismissed South Africa's Andile Phehlukwayo at the 2019 Cricket World Cup; shortened in the same style, he is Ben S

explanation.surface: A text message asks a cricketer whether he is the fielder who made a famous catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'texted' sets the text-speak style: 'Are you' is R U, and Ben Stokes, cut short the way the clue cuts short Andile Phehlukwayo, is BEN S.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Paul Rubens was a Flemish Baroque painter, so he is an artist.

clue.text: As of late, bank must protect foreign money

indicators.note: to protect something is to surround it, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to bank on someone is to rely on them
a cent is a coin used abroad, in the US and the eurozone, rather than in Britain

explanation.surface: A news line saying banks have lately had to safeguard overseas currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean in the period just past, a synonym pair.

clue.text: Blues rock originally developed in France, that is a farce!

indicators.note: letters that develop take on a new shape, so these are rearranged
originally points to the first letter of the word rock

parts.note: que is French for 'that'

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs that blues rock having started in France is ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges BLUES plus R into BURLES; 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A burlesque is a comic parody or mocking imitation, much like a farce.

clue.text: Film genre's most important rule

parts.note: the most important thing is number one, written No. 1 and here read as NO plus the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A claim about the chief convention of a style of film.
explanation.definitionFit: Film noir is the shadowy crime-film style, often just called noir.

clue.text: Fish container placed in front of sailor

indicators.note: says the first piece comes before the second in the answer

parts.note: a skip is a large open bin for rubbish
Jack, as in Jack Tar, is an old name for a sailor

explanation.surface: A fish crate is set down before a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: A skip is the big metal rubbish bin you hire in Britain when clearing a house.
explanation.definitionFit: The skipjack is a species of tuna, so it is a fish.

clue.text: English bank curtailed within borders of Kuwait — that's what IS wants

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other
the borders of a word are its first and last letters
a curtailed word has lost its tail, its last letter

parts.note: Halifax is a British bank, named after the Yorkshire town

explanation.surface: A news-style line about Kuwait's borders and what the Islamic State group is after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' cuts the tail off the bank's name before it goes between the Kuwait borders. IS here is Islamic State, not the verb; Halifax is a Yorkshire town as well as a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A khalifat, a variant spelling of caliphate, is the Islamic state ruled by a caliph that the jihadist group sought to found.

clue.text: Publicity for one who doesn't believe Germany's close to Austria

indicators.note: close to says the next piece sits right beside the one before

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a pagan does not hold the main faith
D is the international vehicle code for Germany
A is the international vehicle code for Austria

explanation.surface: Publicity aimed at an unbeliever, or Germany being near Austria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to' tempts you to take the last letter of Germany; it is a charade indicator putting D right next to A.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is biased information put about to promote a cause, a kind of publicity.

clue.text: Almost 12 having a nap

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: twelve is a dozen

explanation.surface: Nearly noon, and someone is dozing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' cuts the N from A DOZEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoze is an old adjective meaning dozing, asleep lightly.

clue.text: Ice Queen's really impressive

parts.note: to ice someone is slang for murdering them
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of the Queen

explanation.surface: An ice queen, a coldly aloof woman, is said to be stunning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ice Queen' looks like one phrase; it is two pieces, and 's is a link word meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Killer is slang for excellent or formidable, as in a killer outfit.

clue.text: Wrong to pursue criminal record

indicators.note: to pursue is to come after, so the first-named piece goes last

parts.note: Al Capone is the archetypal criminal
bum is slang for bad or wrong, as in a bum note

explanation.surface: Chasing a crook is a mistake on someone's record.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a long-playing record of several tracks.

clue.text: Warm drink

definitions.meaning: a warm, friendly greeting is a hearty one
a sweet fruit concentrate diluted with water, or a liqueur

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both friendly and a sweet diluted fruit drink, two unrelated senses.

clue.text: Mexican native frequently left broken by Beast from the East

indicators.note: a piece broken by another has it pushed into its middle

parts.note: to do something a lot is to do it frequently

indicators.note: in an across entry, coming from the east means reading right to left, backwards

parts.note: an ox is a large beast

explanation.surface: The 'Beast from the East' was the freezing 2018 cold snap in Britain; here it breaks something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beast from the East' reads as the weather nickname, but 'from the East' is a reversal indicator acting on the beast alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The axolotl is a salamander found only in lakes near Mexico City.

clue.text: Christmas has what it says

parts.note: the clue asks what letter the word Christmas lacks; spoken as a phrase, that lack gives a festive word

explanation.walkthrough: The French-derived word for Christmas sounds like 'no L', and that matches the spelling of Christmas, which has no L.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is a word for Christmas, from French Noël.

clue.text: South American's username is hacked

indicators.note: data that has been hacked has been interfered with, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone's online account login has been broken into.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is a link word meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Surinamese means a person from Suriname, a country on South America's north coast.

clue.text: Rock band's performance includes both good and acceptable kind of music

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in another piece
both says two separate letters each go inside
a performance makes the letters perform a new routine, so they are rearranged

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, hence socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A rock group's gig takes in some easy-listening material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performance' rearranges ROCKBAND into BACKROND; 'includes both' puts G and U into it, in two different places.
explanation.definitionFit: Background music is unobtrusive music played behind other activity.

clue.text: Exotic tree as found in piece of land across the pond

indicators.note: one piece is found inside the other

parts.words: piece of land across the pond
parts.note: lot is the American word for a plot of land; 'across the pond' means in America
qua is Latin for 'as', in the capacity of

explanation.surface: An unusual tree growing on a plot in America.
explanation.definitionFit: The loquat is an East Asian evergreen fruit tree, so an exotic one.

clue.text: One blocking fake e-mails causes discomfort

indicators.note: a piece blocking another sits in its path, inside it
fake ones are forged, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: a means one

explanation.surface: A spam filter catching phishing messages causes unease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fake' scrambles EMAILS to MALISE, and A goes inside; 'causes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaise is a general feeling of unease or illness.

clue.text: Important to retain condition for pivotal match

indicators.note: to retain something is to hold it inside

parts.note: a seminal work is highly important and influential
if introduces a condition

explanation.surface: Keeping fit matters for a decisive game.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi-final decides who reaches the final, a crucial match.

clue.text: Uniform for each after overhauling Foreign Office

indicators.note: after says the piece named first comes second in the answer
overhauling something reworks it, so these two letters are rearranged

parts.note: apiece means for each one

explanation.surface: A reform of a government department brings a dress code for every member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overhauling' turns FO into OF.
explanation.definitionFit: Things of a piece are consistent and all alike, so uniform.

clue.text: Mark initially can see hardly at all

parts.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word can

parts.note: Ely, a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, is a bishop's see

explanation.surface: Someone called Mark is barely able to see at first.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is the usual one in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarcely means only just or barely, a synonym pair.

clue.text: Reportedly, slight problem with Sturgeon's speech — time for a break

indicators.note: reportedly tells us the words are heard said aloud

parts.note: Nicola Sturgeon, Scotland's former first minister, would call something slight wee, and a cough is a slight problem with speech

explanation.surface: A report that the Scottish leader's voice is a bit croaky.
explanation.walkthrough: Wee is Scots for small; 'wee cough' said aloud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A week off is a seven-day holiday from work, a break.

clue.text: First man I see naked

parts.note: in the Bible Adam is the first man
in text-message shorthand 'I see' is written IC

explanation.surface: Someone spots the original man without clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First man' looks like the definition, but 'naked' is.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamic can mean unclothed, like Adam in Eden before the Fall.

clue.text: Understudy's part of play on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard, so the words are judged by sound

parts.note: an actor is part of a play's cast

explanation.surface: An understudy takes a role in a radio drama.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic accent, 'actor' and the answer sound close; 's is a link word meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To understudy is to stand in for another performer, to deputise.

clue.text: Indian, perhaps Apache, finally put in old prison

indicators.note: a letter put in goes inside another word

parts.note: can is slang for prison

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word Apache

explanation.surface: An Apache warrior is finally locked up in an old jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian, perhaps' looks like a person, like Apache; it is the Indian Ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian is one example of an ocean, as signalled by 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Select the best red port if choosing kebab for starters

parts.note: cherry red is a bright red

indicators.note: starters are the first letters of the words port, if, choosing and kebab

explanation.surface: A diner picks a red wine, a port, if ordering a kebab.
explanation.definitionFit: To cherry-pick is to choose only the most attractive items.

clue.text: Somewhat relieved if you improve mentally

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone says they'd be a bit relieved if you improved yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: To edify is to instruct someone so as to improve them morally or intellectually.

clue.text: Stretch of Niagara Falls over quite some distance

indicators.note: over means the run is turned over, read backwards
a stretch of the words is a run of letters taken from inside them

explanation.surface: A section of Niagara Falls spans a long way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretch of' takes RAFA from niagaRA FAlls, and 'over' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means at or to a great distance.

clue.text: Sony's second record label, 8?

definitions.note: the answer to 8 down in a particular sense; the question mark signals an example

indicators.note: second picks the second letter of the name Sony

parts.note: RCA is a famous American record label

explanation.surface: Asks whether Sony's other record company is the subject of 8 down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record label' tempts you to think of Sony Music; it is RCA, which Sony does own.
explanation.definitionFit: The orca is the killer whale, so it is an example of the 8-down answer.

clue.text: A Bit of Fry & Laurie, hit and miss

indicators.note: a bit of the word Fry is just its first letter
struck letters are knocked about, so these are scrambled

explanation.surface: A Bit of Fry & Laurie was a British sketch show starring Stephen Fry and Hugh Laurie, said to be uneven in quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Bit of' looks like the show's title; it takes F, and 'hit' scrambles LAURIE into AILURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A miss is an attempt that fails, the opposite of a hit.

clue.text: Discarding wingers, Harry Kane's ultimately preferring mid-field position

indicators.note: dropping the wingers of Harry and Kane removes their outer letters
ultimately takes the last letter of the word preferring
mid takes the middle letter of the word field

explanation.surface: Harry Kane, England's football captain, prefers a midfield role over the wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mid-field position' reads as football; 'position' alone is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange things is to place or position them in order.

clue.text: Dutch painter surely excited to receive Diploma of Art

indicators.note: to receive something is to take it in
excited letters are stirred up, so they are scrambled

parts.note: DA stands for Diploma of Art

explanation.surface: Someone is plainly thrilled to be awarded an art qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges SURELY to RUYSEL, which takes in DA.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob van Ruisdael, also spelt Ruysdael, was a Dutch Golden Age landscape painter.

clue.text: Very narrow lane making one depressed

parts.note: an alley is a narrow lane between buildings

explanation.surface: A tight little backstreet that gets someone down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one depressed' reads as a sad person; it is a sunken thing. 'making' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A valley is a low stretch of land, a depression between hills.
